classification.classification_note: The logical bug is a 255-byte copy into `tlvs[254]`. AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 147` because `ot::Message::Read()` copies message data in chunks and the later 147-byte `memcpy` is the chunk that first crosses the stack redzone.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 1089-byte `ip6-send-fuzzer` witness uses byte 0 only for `settings.mLinkSecurityEnabled`; bytes 1..1088 are appended as a raw IPv6 packet. That packet decodes to a UDP CoAP POST on URI `c/cg`, so `CoapBase::ProcessReceivedRequest()` dispatches it to `Leader::HandleCommissioningGet()`. Inside that handler, the payload-scanning loop eventually reaches bytes `0d ff 05 05 ...` at payload offset 720: type `MeshCoP::Tlv::kGet` followed by raw length byte `0xff`. `MeshCoP::Tlv` inherits `ot::Tlv`, where `0xff` is the extended-length sentinel, and `ot::Tlv::GetLength()` is explicitly documented as incorrect for extended TLVs. The vulnerable code nonetheless stores `255` in local `length` and calls `aMessage.Read(offset + sizeof(MeshCoP::Tlv), length, tlvs)` with stack `uint8_t tlvs[NetworkData::kMaxSize]`, where `NetworkData::kMaxSize` is 254. `Message::Read()` bounds the copy against the source message length but not the destination size, so its chunked `memcpy` overruns `tlvs`; the saved AddressSanitizer report identifies `tlvs` in `HandleCommissioningGet()` as the overflowed stack object and reports the later 147-byte chunk that crosses the redzone. The fix replaces the ad-hoc loop with `Tlv::GetValueOffset()` and stops copying the requester TLV list into a large stack buffer.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the crashing-path MeshCoP TLV header from the request payload.
source.value_from: The staged 1089-byte `poc` is consumed by `tests/fuzz/ip6_send.cpp`: byte 0 only sets `settings.mLinkSecurityEnabled` (`0x20 & 1 == 0` in the saved file), and bytes 1..1088 are appended as a raw IPv6 packet. After IPv6/UDP/CoAP parsing and `/c/cg` resource dispatch, the scanning loop in `HandleCommissioningGet()` reaches payload offset 720 and copies the header bytes `0d ff` into `tlv`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement converts the attacker-controlled raw length byte `0xff` into local `length == 255`, even though `0xff` is the extended-TLV marker rather than a validated base-TLV value length.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing iteration the current TLV header in `tlv` is `0d ff`, read from payload offset 720 of the staged witness.

root_cause.description: The handler copies `length` bytes into stack `tlvs[NetworkData::kMaxSize]` using a fixed 2-byte header and no check that the matched TLV is non-extended or that the requested value fits the 254-byte destination.
root_cause.note: With the witnessed header `0d ff`, step 3 made `length == 255`. The next two bytes are `05 05`, so a proper extended-TLV parse would reject the record instead of treating `0xff` as a base length. The fixing diff replaces this call with `Tlv::GetValueOffset(...)` and removes the large stack copy.

sink.description: ASan sink. `Message::Read()` performs the requested copy into caller buffer `tlvs`, and the later chunk write crosses the end of that 254-byte stack object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 147` at `message.cpp:526` and identifies `tlvs` in `HandleCommissioningGet()` as `[48,302)`. The requested logical copy length is 255 bytes; `Message::Read()` splits it across message-buffer chunks, and the 147-byte chunk is the one that first hits the stack redzone.

parser_admitted.description: CoAP option parsing has already reconstructed URI path `c/cg` from the request options and matched the leader's `mCommissioningDataGet` resource, so execution enters `Leader::HandleCommissioningGet()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. This reads the current MeshCoP TLV header from the CoAP payload into local `tlv`. On the crashing iteration, after the loop has skipped earlier non-`kGet` TLVs, `offset` is 720 and `tlv` receives bytes `0d ff` from the witness payload: type `kGet` plus raw length byte `0xff`.
For the header from step 1, the type comparison succeeds, so this malformed TLV becomes the request's `kGet` record for the subsequent length/copy sequence.

This converts the raw length byte in `tlv` into local `length`. Because the header byte is `0xff`, `length` becomes 255 even though `ot::Tlv::GetLength()` is documented as incorrect for extended TLVs and 255 is the extended-length marker, not a valid base-TLV length.

Root cause. The copy uses a fixed 2-byte `MeshCoP::Tlv` header offset and requests `length == 255` bytes into stack `tlvs[NetworkData::kMaxSize]`, where `NetworkData::kMaxSize == 254`. There is no `!tlv.IsExtended()` or `length <= sizeof(tlvs)` guard, so a malformed extended TLV is treated as a 255-byte base-TLV value copy.

ASan sink. `Message::Read()` bounds the request against the source message length but not the destination buffer. While satisfying step 4's 255-byte request into caller buffer `tlvs`, its chunked `memcpy` overruns the 254-byte stack object; ASan reports the 147-byte chunk that first crosses the redzone.

format.name: OpenThread ip6-send CoAP Commissioner Get request
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 1089 bytes. Byte 0 is only used by the harness for `settings.mLinkSecurityEnabled` (`0x20 & 1 == 0` in the saved file); bytes 1..1088 are appended unchanged as a raw IPv6 packet. That packet must decode to a CoAP POST on URI `c/cg`, and the payload scan in `HandleCommissioningGet()` must eventually read header bytes `0d ff` at the crashing iteration so the code treats a malformed extended `kGet` TLV as a 255-byte base-TLV value and copies it into stack `tlvs[254]`.
